organization.name: Marine Biodiversity Conservation Trust (MBCT)
organization.mission: To conserve and restore marine biodiversity through scientific research, community engagement, and sustainable practices, ensuring healthy oceans for future generations.
organization.about: A registered non-profit charitable trust dedicated to protecting marine life, coral reefs, coastal ecosystems, and ocean biodiversity.
organization.movement: MBCT is a community-driven marine conservation movement led by environmentalists, passionate individuals, and youth volunteers. It brings people from students to scientists together to protect, restore, and sustain marine ecosystems and build a healthy, sustainable blue planet. Its website describes its approach as educating, empowering, and engaging the public through community programs, cleanup drives, and digital awareness campaigns.

programs: Awareness and education programs in schools, colleges, and communities
Beach cleanups and coastal restoration activities
Mangrove restoration, environmental rehabilitation, and youth training
Research and monitoring of marine ecosystems
Partnerships with governments, NGOs, and institutions

objectives.name: Conservation and protection
objectives.details: Protect species, habitats, and ecosystems including coral reefs, mangroves, sea turtles, sharks, and dugongs.

objectives.name: Sustainable use
objectives.details: Encourage responsible fisheries, eco-friendly aquaculture, and better coastal management.

objectives.name: Research and monitoring
objectives.details: Use surveys, species monitoring, habitat checks, and water-quality observations to support evidence-based conservation.

objectives.name: Awareness and education
objectives.details: Build ocean literacy through workshops, school programs, and public campaigns.

objectives.name: Collaboration
objectives.details: Work with governments, NGOs, scientists, and local communities.

major_threats: Plastic pollution harms wildlife and ecosystems.
Overfishing removes key species and disrupts food webs.
Climate change, ocean warming, and acidification contribute to coral bleaching and habitat loss.
Coastal development and dredging can damage mangroves and seagrass beds.
get_involved: The website invites students, educators, and citizens to become volunteers and ocean ambassadors. The chatbot should direct visitors to the official website for current participation and support details.
